sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One reference example. Use it only if you get stuck.

items.prompt: Do an oblique and a right cylinder with the same base and height have equal volume?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 3 and centre O. A point P lies 5 from O. Explain the construction of a tangent from P and give the tangent length.
choices: Draw the circle centred at P with radius 3; the tangent length is 4.
Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 4.
Draw the perpendicular bisector of OP; the tangent length is 4.
Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 2.

items.prompt: An ellipse centred at the origin has foci at (±3, 0) and the sum of distances to the foci equal to 10. Write its equation.
A hyperbola centred at the origin has foci at (±10, 0) and the absolute difference of distances to the foci equal to 12. Write its equation.
Compare a cone and a cylinder with the same base and height. What does Cavalieri’s principle tell us?
choices: They have equal volumes, because every horizontal cross-section has the same area at the same height.
Nothing, because Cavalieri’s principle applies only to prisms.
The cone has one third the volume, which Cavalieri’s principle establishes by comparing cross-sections against a reference solid.
They have equal volumes, and matching cross-sections is exactly how the sphere volume formula is derived.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 7 and centre O. A point P lies 25 from O. Explain the construction of a tangent from P and give the tangent length.
choices: Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 18.
Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 24.
Draw the circle centred at P with radius 7; the tangent length is 24.
Draw the perpendicular bisector of OP; the tangent length is 24.

items.prompt: An ellipse centred at the origin has foci at (±12, 0) and the sum of distances to the foci equal to 26. Write its equation.
A hyperbola centred at the origin has foci at (±5, 0) and the absolute difference of distances to the foci equal to 8. Write its equation.
Compare an oblique cylinder and a right cylinder with the same base area and the same height. What does Cavalieri’s principle tell us?
choices: Nothing, because Cavalieri’s principle applies only to prisms.
The cone has one third the volume, which Cavalieri’s principle establishes by comparing cross-sections against a reference solid.
They have equal volumes, because every horizontal cross-section has the same area at the same height.
They have equal volumes, and matching cross-sections is exactly how the sphere volume formula is derived.
